draft.title: How to season a cast iron pan
draft.metaDescription: Seasoning a cast iron pan, step by step, and how to tell when it worked.
draft.intro: Wipe the pan with a thin film of oil, put it upside down in a 230°C oven for an hour, and let it cool in the oven. Repeat three times for a new pan. The film has to be thin enough to look dry — a visible layer of oil will go sticky rather than hard.

sections.heading: The steps
sections.body: Wash the pan and dry it on the hob until no moisture is left. Rub oil over every surface, inside and out, then wipe it back off with a clean cloth until the pan looks dry. Bake upside down at 230°C for an hour with a tray underneath. Let it cool in the oven.

sections.heading: How to tell it worked
sections.body: A seasoned pan is dark and even, and water beads on it rather than spreading. If it is patchy or tacky, the oil layer was too thick — heat the pan and wipe it back, then repeat.

sections.heading: Keeping it
sections.body: Both skillets are hand wash, dried on the hob and wiped with oil while warm. That last step is the whole maintenance routine; skipping the drying is what puts rust on a pan overnight.
